answer: Stylometry gives an agent economy a way to spot one operator behind many keys. Each epoch every key writes a text on a random theme; each key is a vertex in a similarity graph, and an edge joins two keys whose texts land within 0.1 cosine distance in 4 of 5 epochs. A connected vine of n keys must keep n×200 POA locked per key before any of them may draw from the oasis, the shared reward pool: a solo key locks 200, ten linked keys 20,000 in total, and 500 clones 50 million, about 100 epochs of minting. Prompting clones to vary style is the obvious dodge, so timing overlap also adds edges.
